garage_door_input_group.description: All rates are per EA (each garage door assembly). A garage door assembly is the complete exterior face: all panels, recesses, window inserts (if present), panel edges at articulation joints. Rates are expressed as fixed_time_minutes per EA. Door size (single vs double), panel complexity (flush/raised_panel/carriage), substrate (steel/wood/carriage), and windows (none/standard/divided_lite) are modifiers applied to the EA baseline. Baseline = single-width steel flush door (~60 SF).

task_production_rates.name: Driveway/Apron Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy canvas drop cloths or absorbent mats over driveway/apron. ~18 sec per SF. Canvas ONLY — NO poly sheeting on hardscapes (slippery safety hazard). Heavier than standard poly drops, slower to deploy. Secure edges against wind.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of driveway within overspray zone. Secured against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Taped at edges. Canvas on all traffic areas. Overlap seams.

task_production_rates.name: Adjacent Siding Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply pre-taped poly or masking film to siding panels flanking garage door opening. Tape at casing edge, extend film 4-6 ft beyond opening on each side. ~20 min per single door opening for spray method. Only required for spray application.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete siding coverage. Tape sealed at casing edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Tape sealed tight. Film extends full overspray zone.

task_production_rates.name: Garage Door Window Insert Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply HDPE static-cling film to window inserts in top panel. Edge-seal with UV-resistant tape at glass-to-frame junction. ~20 min baseline per door for standard windows. Divided-lite carriage windows are significantly more time — driven by FAC_GRDR_WINDOWS modifier (standard +45 min, divided_lite +75 min additive).

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete glass coverage. Tape sealed at frame edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Inspect for bleed-through potential. Crisp masking lines.

task_production_rates.name: Weatherstrip Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Push low-tack tape deep into weatherstrip channel along sides and top using putty knife. ~35-40 LF of weatherstrip per standard door. ~18 min per single door. Paint on weatherstripping destroys seal flexibility.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Tape fully seated in channel. No gaps. Complete perimeter (sides + top).
defect_tolerance.QT4: Tape fully seated. Putty knife verification. Complete perimeter. Zero gaps.

task_production_rates.name: Track & Hardware Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask all track and roller contact points, spring mechanism hardware, cables, and brackets. ~18 min per single door. Must NOT be painted — paint causes binding, stalling, potential spring/motor damage. Mask from garage interior side.

defect_tolerance.QT3: ALL moving parts masked. Tracks, rollers, springs, cables, brackets covered.
defect_tolerance.QT4: ALL moving parts masked. Double-check all hardware zones before spray.

task_production_rates.name: Bottom Seal Management
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove bottom weatherseal (astragal) and retainer, or mask in place with tape. ~12 min per door. Preferred: full removal for clean access to bottom panel edge. Alternative: mask + plan for prop during cure. Bottom seal bonds to wet paint if not managed.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Seal removed or masked. Document removal for reinstall.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Seal removed or masked. Document. Verify clean access to bottom panel edge.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Configure airless sprayer with garage-door-specific tips: 310 tip (6-inch fan) for single steel, 412 tip (8-inch fan) for double doors. Install 100-mesh blue filter. Stage 2.5-inch angled sash brush for panel recess detail. Test spray pattern on cardboard. ~25 min per project setup (not per-door).

defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern verified on cardboard.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern at correct distance. Backup tips staged.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Stage brushes for brush-only application: 2.5-inch angled sash for faces and recesses, 2-inch flat for edges. Paint pots and materials. ~12 min. Less setup than spray. Per-project fixed time.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Materials staged within reach.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Materials staged and pre-mixed. Fresh brushes.

task_production_rates.name: Factory Wax Removal (Steel)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Scuff entire steel door face with gray 3M synthetic steel wool pad saturated with biodegradable cleaner. Removes residual factory wax, silicone release agents, and surface contaminants. ~25 min per single door (~60 SF). 2 pads per single door, 3 per double. MANDATORY before any other prep. White rag verification test.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete surface coverage. White rag test — no residue transfer.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete surface coverage. Two-pass minimum. White rag verification documented.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Sand Factory Finish (Steel)

QT3.notes: Even scuff with 120-150 grit. No glossy patches remaining.

QT4.notes: Full surface sand with systematic coverage. Feather all scratches. Raking light verify.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand steel door face with 120-150 grit to degloss factory fluorocarbon/polyester finish. Create mechanical tooth for primer adhesion. Performed AFTER wax removal. ~18-25 min per single door depending on QT.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even scuff pattern. No glossy patches remaining.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full surface sand. All scratches feathered. No gloss under raking light.

task_production_rates.name: ASTM D3359 Adhesion Test (Steel)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Perform ASTM D3359 cross-hatch tape adhesion test on 2-3 locations per door (top, middle, bottom panel). ~8 min per door. Requires lead skill level. If fail (< 4B): escalate to SSPC-SP7 or re-prep. Quality checkpoint before primer.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Test 2-3 locations. Minimum 4B rating. Document pass/fail.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Test 3 locations. Minimum 4B rating. Document with photo.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Wood Garage Door

QT3.notes: Full surface sand. Even scratch pattern. No mill glaze.

QT4.notes: Systematic sand with full coverage. Inspect all edges and recesses. Raking light verify.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand all wood garage door surfaces with 120-150 grit. Remove mill glaze, open grain. Hand sand panel recesses and profiles. Orbital sander for flat panel faces. Include edges accessible through articulation joints. ~30-40 min per single door depending on QT.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full surface sand. Even scratch pattern. No glossy patches.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic sand. All edges and recesses. Raking light verification.

task_production_rates.name: Fill Wood Door Defects

QT4.notes: Fill all defects > 1/16 inch. Sand flush. Verify with raking light.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fill nail holes, minor defects, and small damage with exterior-rated wood filler. Cure, sand flush 150-220 grit. Most NC wood garage doors have minimal defects. ~12-18 min per single door depending on QT.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visible defects filled. Sand flush.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects > 1/16 inch filled. Sand flush. Raking light verify.

task_production_rates.name: Tannin Knot Spot Prime (Wood)

QT3.notes: Spot prime visible knots. Complete seal over each knot.

QT4.notes: Spot prime all knots including small ones. Extended coverage around knot area.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spot-apply alkyd stain-blocking primer to visible knots on tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir). Brush apply to individual knots BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. Severe tannin species may need full-surface application. ~10-15 min per single door depending on knot density and QT.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visible knots sealed. No bleed potential.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All knots sealed including small ones. Extended coverage. No bleed potential.

task_production_rates.name: Carriage-Style Mixed-Material Prep

QT3.notes: Each material prepped per its protocol. No cross-contamination.

QT4.notes: Systematic mixed-material prep. Document overlay surface condition for primer selection.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Prep carriage-style door with mixed materials: steel base (wax removal + degloss), wood/composite overlays (sand per overlay protocol). Assess composite overlays for bonding primer need. Mask decorative hardware and overlay edges to prevent cross-contamination. Lead skill required. ~40-55 min per single door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Each material prepped per its protocol. No cross-contamination.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic prep. Document overlay condition. Cross-contamination prevented.

task_production_rates.name: Dust Removal After Prep
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all sanding dust from garage door surfaces, panel recesses, articulation joints, and edges using tack cloth. ~8 min per single door. Critical to clean articulation joint areas where dust collects.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete dust removal. White rag test on steel.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete dust removal including articulation joints and panel recesses. Zero contamination.

task_production_rates.name: Spray DTM Primer — Steel Garage Door
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray DTM primer on steel door face using airless sprayer with LEAPFROG technique (alternating panels 1,3,5 then 2,4,6, opening joints between). ~18 min per single door including leapfrog joint management. Even wet coat per mfg mil spec. 310 tip for single, 412 for double. CRITICAL: bare metal primed same day as prep.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No holidays. All joints separated. Target 1.5 mils DFT.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No holidays. All joints separated. Uniform mil build. Target 1.5 mils DFT.

task_production_rates.name: Brush DTM Primer — Steel Garage Door
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush apply DTM primer to steel door face with LEAPFROG technique. ~40 min per single door. Approximately 2.2x spray time due to hand application on large flat panels. Brush provides better control on panel recesses but significantly slower for full face.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No drips. Complete coverage. All joints separated.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No drips or brush marks. Complete coverage. Joints separated.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Acrylic Primer — Wood Garage Door
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray 100% acrylic exterior primer on wood door face with LEAPFROG technique. ~20 min per single door. Slightly slower than steel spray due to wood grain absorption — may need heavier wet coat. Six-side sealing obligation (face coat portion — edges/back in separate task).

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No holidays. Leapfrog technique. Adequate wet film build.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No holidays. Leapfrog technique. Uniform mil build. Verify grain sealing.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Acrylic Primer — Wood Garage Door
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush apply acrylic primer to wood door face with LEAPFROG technique. ~45 min per single door. Brush provides better grain penetration in recesses but significantly slower. ~2.25x spray time.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No drips. Complete coverage including edges at joints.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No drips or brush marks. Complete coverage. Grain penetration verified.

task_production_rates.name: Bonding Primer — Carriage Composite Overlays
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush apply bonding primer to glossy/sealed composite overlay panels on carriage-style doors. ~20 min per single door. Overlay surfaces only — steel base gets DTM separately. Conditional on glossy composite surfaces. Must topcoat within 1 week.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete overlay coverage. No holidays on composite surfaces.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete overlay coverage. Uniform film. No holidays. Document topcoat deadline.

task_production_rates.name: Six-Side Seal Primer — Wood Door Edges and Back Face
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush primer on all hidden surfaces per DASMA TDS #162: back face (garage-interior side), top edge, bottom edge, side edges. End-grain absorbs more — heavier application at edges. ~35 min per single door including back face access (prop door open or paint panels individually). Six-side seal failure causes moisture wicking, rot, panel distortion, warranty voidance.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage all 6 sides. Heavy at end-grain edges.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete six-side coverage. Flashlight/mirror inspect. No holidays at edges or back face.

task_production_rates.name: Spray First Finish Coat — Garage Door Face

QT3.notes: LEAPFROG. Even coat, no runs/sags. Verify no joint bridging.

QT4.notes: LEAPFROG. Even coat with premium material. Inspect for holidays. Raking light before dry.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray first finish coat on garage door exterior face using airless sprayer with LEAPFROG technique (alternating panels, open joints, tack-free between). ~18-22 min per single door including joint management. 310 tip for single, 412 for double. Do NOT back-roll on metal — orange peel is undesirable.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No runs, sags, or holidays. All joints separated.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. Zero defects visible. All joints separated. Uniform mil build.

task_production_rates.name: Brush First Finish Coat — Garage Door Face

QT3.notes: LEAPFROG. Even coat, no lap marks. Clean edges.

QT4.notes: LEAPFROG. Even coat. Tip off brush marks while wet.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush first finish coat on garage door face with LEAPFROG technique. ~45-55 min per single door. Approximately 2.5x spray time. Maintain wet edge, long even strokes. Use only when spray is not feasible.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No lap marks. All joints separated.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No lap marks or brush marks. Tip off while wet. Joints separated.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Panel Recesses — First Finish Coat

QT3.notes: Complete recess coverage. No puddles in corners.

QT4.notes: Thin even coat. No buildup at panel-to-face transition.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish coat into panel recesses on raised-panel and carriage-style doors. Work recesses BEFORE face spray for wet-on-wet blend at transition. ~12-18 min per single door depending on QT. Carriage overlay detail (crossbuck grooves, hardware surrounds) adds time via panel complexity modifier.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete recess coverage. No puddles. Clean transition to face.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Thin even coat. No buildup at panel-to-face transition.

task_production_rates.name: Leapfrog Joint Separation Verification — Coat 1
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: After first coat application, verify all articulation joints are free and not bridged. Manually articulate each panel joint. ~5 min per single door (~4-5 joints). If bridged, immediately break bond while wet. MANDATORY quality gate — joint bridging causes catastrophic paint tearing and opener motor damage.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Every joint articulated. No bridging. Wet bridges broken immediately.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Every joint articulated. No bridging. Wet bridges broken immediately.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Inspection

QT3.notes: Visual scan for obvious defects. Verify joint separation.

QT4.notes: Raking light inspection. Mark all defects. Check recesses. Verify joint separation.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Inspect first finish coat for runs, sags, drips, holidays, dust nibs. Check for paint bridging at articulation joints. Mark defects for repair. QT3: visual scan. QT4: raking light. ~5-10 min per single door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Identify obvious defects for repair. Joints confirmed free.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Raking light — all defects identified and marked. Joints confirmed. Recesses checked.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Sand (QT4 Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light scuff sand between finish coats with 220-grit. QT4 ONLY — QT3 skips sanding. Hand sand panel recesses, orbital for flat faces. ~20 min per single door. Promotes intercoat adhesion and removes minor defects.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Light scuff. Even scratch pattern. Include panel recesses. No aggressive sanding.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Defect Repair

QT3.notes: Sand out obvious runs/sags. Spot-coat holidays.

QT4.notes: Full defect repair. Feather all repairs. Re-inspect.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Repair defects found during intercoat inspection: sand runs/sags, spot-coat holidays, feather drip marks. Address paint buildup in recesses or at joint edges. ~5-10 min per single door depending on QT and defect count.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects repaired. Runs sanded smooth.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired. Feathered smooth. Re-inspect after repair.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all sanding dust after intercoat sanding. Tack cloth all surfaces including recesses and joints. QT4 ONLY — accompanies intercoat sanding. ~6 min per single door.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete dust removal. Tack cloth all surfaces including articulation joints.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Second Finish Coat — Garage Door Face

QT3.notes: LEAPFROG. Even coat. Final visual check. Verify no joint bridging.

QT4.notes: LEAPFROG. Even coat with premium material. Raking light before dry. Zero defects.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray second finish coat. Same LEAPFROG technique as coat 1. Same tip and material. Final coat — extra care on even coverage and complete film build. ~18-22 min per single door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No runs, sags, or holidays. All joints separated.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. Zero defects. All joints separated. Uniform film build.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Second Finish Coat — Garage Door Face

QT3.notes: LEAPFROG. Even coat, no lap marks.

QT4.notes: LEAPFROG. Even coat. Tip off brush marks while wet.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush second finish coat. Same LEAPFROG technique as coat 1. Final coat — maintain wet edge. ~45-55 min per single door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No lap marks. All joints separated.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No lap marks or brush marks. Joints separated. Final coat quality.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Panel Recesses — Second Finish Coat

QT4.notes: Thin even coat. No buildup at transitions. Uniform film.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush second finish coat into panel recesses. Same technique as coat 1: recesses before face spray for wet-on-wet blend. ~12-18 min per single door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete recess coverage. No puddles.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Thin even coat. No buildup at transitions. Uniform film.

task_production_rates.name: Leapfrog Joint Separation Verification — Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: After second coat, verify all articulation joints are free. Same mandatory quality gate as coat 1. ~5 min per single door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Every joint articulated. No bridging.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Every joint articulated. No bridging. Documented.

task_production_rates.name: Prop Door Open for Bottom Seal Cure
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Prop garage door 2-4 inches above driveway threshold to prevent bottom seal bonding to wet paint. Use shims, blocks, or opener chain adjustment. ~5 min per door. Prevents common callback — seal stuck to driveway tears paint and seal. Inform homeowner of 24-48 hr cure window.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Door propped 2-4 inches. Stable prop. Homeowner informed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Door propped 2-4 inches. Stable prop. Homeowner informed of timeline.

task_production_rates.name: Final Door Inspection

QT3.notes: Visual scan all panels. Verify joint separation. Check bottom seal prop. Mark touch-ups.

QT4.notes: Raking light inspection all panels. Uniform sheen verification. Joint separation. Window masking lines.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final visual inspection of completed garage door: all panels, articulation joints, recesses, window masking lines (if present), hardware zone masking lines. Verify complete coverage, uniform sheen. ~8-15 min per door depending on QT.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All panels inspected. Joints separated. Bottom seal clearance verified.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Raking light on all panels. Uniform sheen. All masking lines clean. Joints separated.

task_production_rates.name: Balance Test Checkpoint
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: SOP quality gate (not billable): verify garage door balance after painting. Disconnect opener, manual lift to halfway, release — should stay. If unbalanced, flag for spring adjustment (not painting scope). ~5 min per door. Lead skill level required for safety.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Balance test performed. Result documented. If fail: flagged for customer.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Balance test performed. Result documented with photo. If fail: flagged with recommendation.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Minor Defects

QT3.notes: Address obvious defects. Feather into surrounding.

QT4.notes: Address all marked defects. Invisible feather. Re-inspect after touch-up.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch up minor defects found during final inspection: small holidays, drips at panel edges, masking bleed-through at windows. Brush touch-up with matching finish. Feather into surrounding area. ~8-15 min per door depending on QT and defect count.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects addressed. Touch-ups feathered.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects addressed. Invisible feather. Re-inspected after repair.

task_production_rates.name: Window Masking Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove HDPE static-cling film and edge tape from window inserts. Remove tape at angle to prevent paint film lifting. Clean adhesive residue from glass. Inspect paint line quality. ~10 min per door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Masking removed. Glass clean. Paint line acceptable.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Masking removed at angle. Glass clean. Sharp paint line at frame edge.

task_production_rates.name: Weatherstrip Tape Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove protective tape from weatherstrip channels (sides + top). Verify no paint contamination on weatherstripping. ~8 min per door. If paint found, clean immediately — dried paint on weatherstrip causes seal failure.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete tape removal. No paint on weatherstripping.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete tape removal. Verified no paint contamination. Seal flexibility confirmed.

task_production_rates.name: Track & Hardware Masking Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove tape and plastic from track, roller, spring, and cable hardware. Verify no paint on moving parts or contact surfaces. ~8 min per door. Paint on track/rollers causes binding — clean immediately.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete masking removal. ZERO paint on moving parts.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete masking removal. ZERO paint on moving parts. Track and rollers verified clean.

task_production_rates.name: Adjacent Siding Masking Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove masking film and tape from siding panels adjacent to garage door opening. Fold paint-side-in. Verify no drips/overspray on siding. ~10 min per door. Only applicable for spray method.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Masking removed. No overspray on siding.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Masking removed. Fold paint-side-in. No overspray on siding. Siding inspected.

task_production_rates.name: Bottom Seal Reinstallation
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Reinstall bottom weatherseal (astragal) and retainer if removed during setup. Only after 24-48 hr cure. Verify seal compression against driveway threshold. If masked in place, remove prop blocks and lower door. ~12 min per door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Seal correctly seated. Proper compression against threshold.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Seal correctly seated. Proper compression verified. No paint bonding seal to driveway.

task_production_rates.name: Driveway Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove canvas drops from driveway/apron. Fold paint-side-in. Verify no drips on driveway surface. ~12 sec per SF. Faster than setup (no taping required). Clean any drips immediately — dried paint on broom-finish concrete is nearly impossible to remove.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Canvas removed. Fold paint-side-in. No paint on driveway.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Canvas removed. Fold paint-side-in. Driveway inspected for drips. Clean residue.

task_production_rates.name: Door Articulation Test
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Full open/close cycle test. Reconnect opener. Open, stop at midpoint, close. Listen for unusual sounds. Verify no paint bridging at any joint and no binding. ~5 min per door. Final quality gate.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full cycle — no binding, no tearing, no unusual sounds.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full cycle — no binding, no tearing, no unusual sounds. Opener functions normally.

task_production_rates.name: Tool and Equipment Cleaning
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean all brushes, spray equipment (flush lines, clean tip and filter). Shape and store brushes. Flush airless sprayer with water (latex materials). Dispose of used synthetic steel wool pads. ~20 min per project (not per-door).

defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment cleaned. Brushes shaped. Spray lines flushed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment cleaned. Brushes shaped and stored. Spray lines flushed. Steel wool disposed.

factor_modifiers.name: Garage Door Size Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Primary EA-to-time scaling factor. Double door is ~1.85x single (not exactly 2x because setup/cleanup is fixed per door opening, not per SF).
factor_modifiers.notes: Single door baseline (~56-63 SF face area). Double door (~112-126 SF). 1.85x reflects that face area approximately doubles but setup/cleanup per opening is fixed. Applied to all per-EA tasks. Equipment setup (FIXED tasks) are NOT affected.
factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Multiplicative with other modifiers. Door size is typically the largest single modifier.

factor_modifiers.name: Panel Complexity Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Production rate modifier for panel detail work. Flush panels = baseline. Raised-panel and carriage add brush detail time.
factor_modifiers.notes: Flush = continuous spray/brush surface. Raised_panel = +10% for brush work in panel recesses. Carriage = +30% for meticulous masking, multi-tone cutting, overlay detail. Carriage range per doctrine is 1.25-1.40x — using 1.30x as calibration starting point. Does NOT apply to protection setup/teardown or inspection tasks.
factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Multiplicative with door_size and substrate modifiers.

factor_modifiers.name: Window Masking Additive Time
factor_modifiers.description: ADDITIVE time modifier for window masking — NOT multiplicative. Independent of panel complexity.
factor_modifiers.notes: Additive time in MINUTES per door. Standard = small window inserts in top panel. Divided-lite = carriage-style divided-lite patterns requiring individual pane masking. Range per doctrine: 0.5-1.5 hrs (30-90 min). Standard = 45 min, divided_lite = 75 min. Window masking and unmasking are the primary tasks affected. Window tasks only activate when panel_type includes 'windows'.
factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Additive — added to base task time BEFORE multiplicative modifiers. Door size modifier then applies to the sum.

factor_modifiers.name: Substrate Material Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Substrate material modifier affecting prep and prime task rates.
factor_modifiers.notes: Steel = baseline (wax removal + degloss included in base rate). Wood = +15% (six-side seal obligation per DASMA TDS #162 + grain management). Carriage = +25% (mixed materials + overlay detail). Does NOT apply to finish coat tasks — after priming, surface is normalized. Applies primarily to prep and prime module tasks.
factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Multiplicative with door_size and panel_complexity. Applied to prep and prime tasks only.

factor_modifiers.name: Quality Tier Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier modifier for tasks that use qt_scaled classification. QT3 is baseline.
factor_modifiers.notes: QT3 = baseline (1.00). QT4 = selective_multiplier (1.15) on qt_scaled tasks — slower pace, tighter tolerances, more thorough inspection. Applied via qt_rates structure on individual tasks. Binary tasks are NOT affected — same rate at both tiers. No additional_rounds mechanism — both tiers get 2 finish coats.
factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Already embedded in qt_rates per task. Not applied separately at engine level for qt_scaled tasks. For binary tasks, QT modifier does not apply.

factor_modifiers.name: Exterior Access Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Access type modifier per exterior doctrine. Garage doors are ground-level, so baseline applies. Included for completeness — engine may need it for unusual configurations.
factor_modifiers.notes: Garage doors are virtually always ground-level access (1.00 baseline). Ladder/scaffold/lift values included per exterior doctrine mandate but should rarely if ever apply to garage door work. FAC_HEIGHT is NOT used for exterior — FAC_EXT_ACCESS replaces it per estimation engineer agent doctrine.
factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Multiplicative with all other modifiers. Max combined modifier cap: 4.0x.

factor_modifiers.name: Exterior Substrate Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Substrate condition modifier for prep tasks. NC context means substrate is in factory/new condition.
factor_modifiers.notes: NC context: substrate is new/factory condition (1.00 baseline). Fair/poor values included for edge cases (transit damage, weather exposure before painting). Applies to prep module tasks only — prime/finish rates are unaffected (prep normalizes surface).
factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Multiplicative with substrate and access modifiers.

factor_modifiers.name: Wind Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Wind condition modifier — high wind blocks spray, forces brush/roll rate.
factor_modifiers.notes: Calm = baseline. Moderate = 10% time increase (overspray management). High = STOP SPRAY — must switch to brush application method. Spray tasks include site_condition_rules that exclude when wind_condition = high. Per exterior doctrine mandate.
factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Multiplicative. High wind forces method switch, not rate adjustment.

factor_modifiers.name: Sun Exposure Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Sun exposure modifier — full sun forces early scheduling, reduces daily productive hours.
factor_modifiers.notes: Full sun on garage door face (typically south or west facing) accelerates dry time, reducing working window for leapfrog technique. 10% time increase reflects schedule compression. Shade/partial_sun = baseline. Garage doors are often recessed in garage opening which provides some shade.

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Temperature Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Surface temperature modifier — cold/hot extend recoat intervals and affect working window.
factor_modifiers.notes: Normal (50-90F surface) = baseline. Cold surface (< 50F) = 15% time increase (extended recoat, slower cure, risk of fish-eye). Hot surface (> 90F) = 10% increase (flash dry, lap marks, premature skinning during leapfrog). Steel doors heat up faster than wood — surface temp modifier is critical for south/west-facing steel doors.
factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Multiplicative with other environmental modifiers. Max combined environmental: ~1.35x.

rounds.description: All garage doors get prime + 2 finish coats regardless of quality tier. No additional_rounds mechanism. Round config: ROUND_GRDR_PRIME_2FINISH.

qt_scaled_behavior.QT3: Baseline rates. Production pace. Visual inspection.
qt_scaled_behavior.QT4: 1.15x time on qt_scaled tasks. Raking light inspection. Intercoat sand (220-grit). Premium materials. Tighter defect tolerance.

qt_conditional_tasks.notes: Intercoat dust removal — accompanies QT4 sanding

time_summary.description: Estimated total time for baseline scenario: single-width steel flush garage door, spray method, QT3. Times are per-EA before modifiers.

phase_totals_minutes.setup_breakdown: driveway_protect(variable SF) + siding_mask(20) + weatherstrip(18) + track_hardware(18) + bottom_seal(12) + equip_setup_spray(25) = ~93 min + driveway SF time
phase_totals_minutes.interstage_breakdown: inspect_intercoat_QT3(5) + repair_intercoat_QT3(5) = 10 min (no sand at QT3)
phase_totals_minutes.cleanup_breakdown: weatherstrip_unmask(8) + track_hardware_unmask(8) + bottom_seal_reinstall(12) + driveway_teardown(variable) + articulation_test(5) + tool_clean(20) = ~53 min (siding_unmask 10 for spray)
phase_totals_minutes.notes: Baseline ~4.8 hours for single steel flush QT3 spray. Excludes driveway SF protection time. Add ~0.5-1 hr for driveway protection (typical 100-200 SF at 200 SF/hr). Total realistic: ~5.3-5.8 hrs for single steel flush QT3 spray.

modifier_impact_examples.modifier: FAC_GRDR_SUBSTRATE = 1.15 + wood tasks replace steel tasks

modifier_impact_examples.scenario: Single steel flush + windows QT3 spray
modifier_impact_examples.modifier: FAC_GRDR_WINDOWS standard = +45 min mask, +10 min unmask

assumptions.value: All fixed_time_minutes are for single-width steel flush door (~60 SF) baseline
assumptions.source: User-provided rate guidance + exterior door sibling calibration
assumptions.note: Rates aligned to user guidance: total baseline single steel ~120-180 min (2-3 hrs) for core painting tasks. Total including setup/cleanup/inspect runs higher (~287 min / 4.8 hrs).

assumptions.value: Brush application ~2.2-2.5x spray time for garage door face tasks
assumptions.source: Industry standard + exterior door sibling pattern
assumptions.note: Large flat panels are ideal for spray — brush is very slow. Ratio consistent with exterior door spec brush/spray delta.

assumptions.value: ~30% of spray/brush time is leapfrog joint management (open, verify tack-free, close)
assumptions.source: Garage door doctrine + professional painting practice
assumptions.note: No doctrine quantifies leapfrog overhead. Estimated 30% of application time for sectional door joint management. Built into per-EA rates.

assumptions.source: Exterior door walkway protect sibling + canvas material weight factor
assumptions.note: Canvas drops are heavier than standard poly — slower to deploy. Sibling walkway protect rate is 250 SF/hr. Garage driveway slightly slower (200 SF/hr) due to larger contiguous area and canvas weight.

assumptions.value: 35 min per single wood door for back face + edges
assumptions.source: DASMA TDS #162 requirement + professional painting practice
assumptions.note: No doctrine quantifies six-side sealing time. Estimated from back face access difficulty (prop door, brush interior side) + all 4 edges with heavier end-grain application.

assumptions.value: 5 min per door — SOP quality gate, not billable
assumptions.note: Quick safety test. Disconnect opener, manual lift, release at midpoint. If unbalanced, flag for customer — spring adjustment is not painting scope.

risks.description: Wax removal may take significantly longer on doors with heavy factory finish or multiple protective coatings
risks.impact: Prep time could increase 50-100% on wax removal task
risks.mitigation: Rate range accounts for variability (20-30 min). Chemical degreaser alternative if manual scuffing is insufficient.

risks.description: Leapfrog technique timing is weather-sensitive — hot weather accelerates tack and may not allow enough time between alternating panels
risks.impact: May need to reduce panels per pass or wait longer between passes, increasing total time 15-25%
risks.mitigation: FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP modifier accounts for some of this. Schedule early morning for south/west-facing doors.

risks.description: Carriage-style doors have high time variability depending on overlay material and complexity
risks.impact: Carriage modifier range is 1.25-1.40x. Using 1.30x as default may under- or over-estimate by 5-10%
risks.mitigation: Field calibration priority. Rate ranges provided. FAC_GRDR_PANEL_COMPLEXITY adjustable per project.

risks.description: Six-side sealing on wood doors requires back face access which may be difficult depending on door installation
risks.impact: Back face access time is highly variable — could add 15-30 min if panels must be individually detached
risks.mitigation: 35 min estimate includes typical prop-door access. If individual panel detach is required, escalate to separate scope item.

risks.description: Bottom seal reinstallation return visit after 24-48 hr cure adds mobilization cost
risks.impact: Return visit for bottom seal + final articulation test. Minimum 30-60 min mobilization overhead.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with other exterior work return visits. Bottom seal + articulation test is ~17 min labor — mobilization dominates.

validation_plan.calibration_target: Adjust base rates if actual falls outside 4.5-6.5 hr window

validation_plan.description: Time double-width steel flush door and compare to single-door-time x 1.85
Time wax removal task independently on factory-primed steel door
validation_plan.calibration_target: Validate 25 min baseline. Adjust if consistently faster/slower.

validation_plan.description: Time carriage-style door end-to-end vs steel flush baseline
Time wood door six-side seal task independently
validation_plan.calibration_target: Validate 35 min baseline. Highly variable — may need condition-based sub-rates.

validation_plan.description: Time brush-only finish coat vs spray finish coat on same door type
validation_plan.calibration_target: Validate brush/spray ratio of ~2.5x for face tasks

validation_plan.description: Time window masking for standard vs divided-lite configurations
validation_plan.expected_range: Standard: 60-70 min total (20 base + 45 additive). Divided-lite: 95-100 min.
